candidate.title: Add cache hit/miss ratio reporting
candidate.problem_statement: Developers need to monitor the efficiency of their caches beyond raw hit/miss counts. Providing a calculated hit ratio directly in the CacheInfo or via a helper helps in tuning maxsize or TTL values.
requirements: Extend the internal tracking of decorators to support calculating a hit ratio.
Add a hit_ratio property to the object returned by cache_info().
The hit_ratio is defined as hits / (hits + misses).
If total accesses (hits + misses) is zero, the hit_ratio must be 0.0.
The ratio should be a float rounded to 4 decimal places.
acceptance_criteria: Calling a @cached function 2 times with hits and 2 times with misses results in a hit_ratio of 0.5.
Calling cache_info() on a fresh cache returns a hit_ratio of 0.0.
The hit_ratio is accessible as an attribute on the CacheInfo namedtuple.
candidate.existing_behaviour: CacheInfo only contains hits, misses, maxsize, and currsize. There is no automated calculation of efficiency metrics.
edge_cases: Division by zero when hits and misses are both 0.
Precision handling for very high hit rates.

contract.name: CacheInfo.hit_ratio
contract.behaviour: Returns the ratio of hits to total accesses (hits + misses) rounded to 4 decimal places.

candidate.title: Add a peek method for non-mutating access
candidate.problem_statement: In LRU or LFU caches, accessing an item via __getitem__ or get() modifies the cache state (reordering or incrementing frequency). Users sometimes need to check a value without affecting its eviction priority.
requirements: Add a 'peek' method to the Cache base class.
For LRUCache, 'peek' returns the value but does NOT move the key to the 'most recently used' position.
For LFUCache, 'peek' returns the value but does NOT increment its access count.
For TTLCache, 'peek' returns the value but does NOT trigger expiration of the key (though it may still return None or raise KeyError if already expired).
Signature should match 'get(key, default=None)'.
acceptance_criteria: In an LRUCache of size 2, peeking at the oldest item, then adding a new item, should still evict the peeked item.
In an LFUCache, peeking at an item multiple times does not change its position in the popitem() order relative to items that were naturally accessed.
If the key is not present, return the default value.
candidate.existing_behaviour: All access methods (get, __getitem__) are considered 'hits' and update the eviction metadata of the cache.
edge_cases: Peeking at an item that is technically expired in TTLCache but not yet removed.
Peeking in a FIFOCache (where it has no effect on order anyway).

contract.name: Cache.peek
contract.signature: def peek(self, key: Any, default: Any = None) -> Any
contract.behaviour: Returns the value associated with the key without updating eviction metadata (like LRU rank or LFU frequency).

candidate.title: Add expiring-soon callback to TTLCache
candidate.problem_statement: In some systems, when an item expires, it needs to be cleaned up (e.g., closing a network socket or deleting a temp file). TTLCache should allow a callback to be executed right before an item is evicted due to TTL expiration.
requirements: Add an optional 'on_expire' parameter to TTLCache.__init__.
on_expire must be a callable that accepts (key, value).
The callback must be triggered during any operation that causes items to expire (get, set, expire, popitem).
The callback must be triggered AFTER the item is removed from the internal mapping but before the initiating method returns.
Exceptions raised in the callback should be propagated to the caller.
acceptance_criteria: Initializing TTLCache(maxsize=10, ttl=60, on_expire=my_callback) and letting an item expire triggers my_callback(key, value).
Manual calls to cache.expire() trigger the callback for each expired item.
The callback is not triggered for manual deletions via pop() or __delitem__.
candidate.existing_behaviour: TTLCache silently removes expired items during access or eviction.
edge_cases: Callback raising an exception during a 'get' call.
Callback modifying the cache itself (should be discouraged but handled safely if possible, or documented as undefined).
Expiration of multiple items at once.

contract.name: TTLCache.__init__
contract.signature: def __init__(self, maxsize, ttl, timer=time.monotonic, getsizeof=None, on_expire=None)
contract.behaviour: Initializes a TTLCache with an optional callback for expired items.

candidate.title: Support key-specific TTL overrides
candidate.problem_statement: Not all data is equal; some items in a TTLCache might need to persist longer than others (e.g., static config vs dynamic session data). Currently, TTLCache uses a global TTL.
requirements: Allow the 'set' operation to optionally specify a TTL that overrides the cache default for that specific key.
Since __setitem__ does not support extra arguments, add a 'insert' method to TTLCache.
The 'insert' method accepts (key, value, ttl=None).
If ttl is None, the cache's default TTL is used.
The specific TTL should be stored alongside the item and used by the expiration logic.
Retrieving the item via __getitem__ should still use its specific expiration timestamp.
acceptance_criteria: cache.insert('key', 'value', ttl=3600) persists the item for an hour even if the cache default is 60 seconds.
The 'ttl' property of the cache remains the default value for other items.
Items with specific TTLs are still evicted if maxsize is reached, following the LRU-order within TTLCache.
candidate.existing_behaviour: All items in a TTLCache share the same TTL duration from the moment they are inserted or updated.
edge_cases: Updating an existing key with a different TTL.
Setting a TTL of 0 (should expire immediately).

contract.name: TTLCache.insert
contract.signature: def insert(self, key: Any, value: Any, ttl: Optional[float] = None) -> None
contract.behaviour: Inserts an item into the cache with an optional per-key TTL override.

candidate.title: Enforce strict capacity validation
candidate.problem_statement: Users sometimes initialize caches with invalid maxsize values (e.g., negative numbers or non-numeric types) which leads to unpredictable behavior during eviction. We need a consistent validation layer at initialization for all cache types.
requirements: All Cache subclasses must validate maxsize during __init__.
maxsize must be a number (int or float) greater than or equal to 0.
If getsizeof is provided, it must be a callable.
If maxsize is not a valid number or is negative, raise a ValueError with a descriptive message.
If getsizeof is not a callable and not None, raise a TypeError.
acceptance_criteria: Cache(maxsize=0) is accepted and behaves as an empty cache that evicts immediately.
candidate.existing_behaviour: Cache and its subclasses currently accept maxsize without validation, potentially leading to errors only when the cache grows or eviction is triggered.

contract.name: ValidationError
contract.behaviour: Exception raised when cache configuration parameters are invalid.

candidate.title: Implement cache warm-up capability
candidate.problem_statement: When deploying new application versions, caches are cold, leading to performance spikes. A standard 'update' or 'load' method that bypasses some eviction logic or performs bulk insertions safely is needed.
requirements: Add a 'load' method to the Cache class to support bulk insertion of items.
The method should accept an iterable of (key, value) pairs.
Items should be added in the order they appear in the iterable.
If the number of items exceeds maxsize, the standard eviction policy of the specific Cache subclass (LRU, FIFO, etc.) must be applied during loading.
The method must be atomic if a lock is provided to the decorator (though the base method is on the Cache class itself).
acceptance_criteria: cache.load([('a', 1), ('b', 2)]) populates the cache with both items.
Loading more than maxsize items into an LRUCache results in only the most recent items remaining.
Loading returns the number of items successfully stored.
candidate.existing_behaviour: Users must manually loop and use __setitem__, which doesn't convey intent and might be less efficient for bulk operations in subclasses.
edge_cases: Loading duplicate keys within the same load call (last one wins).
Loading items that are larger than maxsize if getsizeof is used.

contract.name: Cache.load
contract.signature: def load(self, iterable: Iterable[Tuple[Any, Any]]) -> int
contract.behaviour: Bulk loads items into the cache and returns the count of items currently in the cache after operation.
